key_insight: Spherical propeller forcing produces a purely forward energy cascade across the analyzed scales, while energy flux remains direction-dependent despite nearly isotropic energy statistics.
engineering_relevance: The findings inform the design and operation of turbulence chambers by linking forcing geometry and propeller frequency to turbulent energy transfer and key flow scales.
method: Apply the Kármán–Howarth–Monin framework without assuming isotropy.
Analyze temporal fluctuations under low-mean-flow conditions where Taylor’s frozen-turbulence hypothesis does not apply.
Develop a propeller-frequency scaling framework using measurements from this device and previously reported HIT chambers.
evidence_signal: Measurements show orientation-averaged structure functions consistent with Kolmogorov’s two-thirds law and an intermediate-scale Eulerian frequency spectrum supporting Tennekes’ prediction.
watch_item: Nearly isotropic energy statistics do not guarantee isotropic energy transfer; residual forcing asymmetries can remain visible in directional flux.
paper_title: Interscale energy transfer in a propeller-driven homogeneous and isotropic turbulence generation device
